Pose-driven sprites

How the Drifter's run cycles went from "the model guesses the stride" to "we hand it the stride": a Mixamo skeleton drives Wan 2.2 Animate, the painted still supplies the look, and every driver frame becomes exactly one sprite frame.

The problem

Until now a run cycle was a free image-to-video clip of the still ("running in place, treadmill, static camera") from which a cutter picked one stride by comparing silhouettes. Seen from the front, back or side a left step and a right step have the same silhouette, so the period was ambiguous by a factor of two and the cutter often picked the wrong one: six frames holding two steps, or half a stride stretched over a full cycle. Only the diagonals, where the two legs look different, came out right every time.

The method

  1. A real stride. Garry downloaded Mixamo's Running (and Walking, Pain Gesture) as FBX, 30 fps, "In Place". One file is exactly one stride, 21 frames, and its last frame lands on its first.
  2. Drivers per view. tools/pose_driver.py runs inside Blender: it reads the skeleton, works out which way the figure faces from its feet, turns it to each of the game's five views (back, back-diagonal, side, front-diagonal, front; the side and diagonals facing screen-right like the painted stills), looks at it from a camera 25° above (the game camera is high), resamples the stride to 24 frames and adds a 25th that repeats the first. A second, plain-Python pass draws the joints as OpenPose skeletons, the format Wan Animate is trained on. Face and ear points are only drawn when that side of the head faces the camera.
  3. Wan 2.2 Animate. The character still goes in as the reference image (through CLIP-Vision and as a latent), the skeleton frames as the pose video. The model repaints the still following the motion. The 4-step distillation LoRA makes a 640×640×25 clip take about a minute on the R9700.
  4. No detection. Every output frame is keyed (chroma key with despill), cropped to one shared box so the bounce survives, outlined, scaled to the standing still, and packed straight into the strip. There is nothing left to guess: 24 in, 24 out, same cadence in all five views.
  5. One-shots the same way. The hit reaction is the Mixamo pain gesture sliced from 0.2 s to 1.0 s into 9 frames, rendered per view and played through once when the hero is hit. The drivers carry both hands with every finger in the DWPose style (the Mixamo rig has the finger bones), which is what stopped the model from guessing where the hands go.

Things that had to be dealt with

Which way is forward. Mixamo rigs do not agree on a facing axis, so the driver works it out from the feet (toe minus ankle, averaged over the stride) rather than assuming one.

Which way is right. The first drivers turned the figure the wrong way about the vertical axis, so every side and diagonal cycle came out facing screen-left; in the game, which mirrors the right-facing views when the hero runs left, that inverted left and right. Fixed by flipping the sign of the turn; the three affected views were re-rendered.

Invented faces. Wan Animate painted a face and hair behind Astro's opaque visor in the front view. The character JSON now carries anim_hint (what the animation must keep) and anim_negative (what it must not invent), passed as the prompt hint and negative prompt of every clip.

Speed. 24 frames covered the stride in 0.86 s at 28 fps, slower than the Mixamo run; playback is 36 fps now (0.67 s, the clip's own tempo), frames unchanged.

Effects out of nowhere. Describing the hit as "flinching from a hit" made the model paint impact rings and a white blade around the Drifter. Hit clips now describe the body only ("staggering and recoiling backwards, then straightening up") and ban effects in the negative prompt.

Loop length. Wan wants 4k+1 frames. Loops render 25 with the last a repeat of the first and drop it; one-shots render 9.

What stays on the old path

Creatures without a human skeleton (ants, cacti, beetles, the scorpion, the tumbleweed) still use the free clip and the silhouette cutter. The goblin family and the dust mummy could move to the Orc Walk and Walking drivers; the beetle to Big Guy Walking.
